name: Uran-6

key_facts.label: Protection
key_facts.value: Tracked, remotely operated, interchangeable mine-clearing attachment

characteristics: Tracked, remotely operated, interchangeable mine-clearing attachment
Strength: Combat-proven across multiple conflicts (Syria, Nagorno-Karabakh 2020, Ukraine since 2022) rather than an experimental/exhibition-only system
Limitation: Purpose-limited to mine clearance; not a combat or logistics platform
Estimated quantity available: Fielded numbers not disclosed
employment_notes: One of the few Russian UGV types with an actual multi-conflict deployment record predating this war, rather than being purpose-built or first fielded in Ukraine
contrast_vs_traditional: Remote mine clearance is one of the oldest unmanned-ground-vehicle roles precisely because it was always understood as too dangerous for a person to do repeatedly — the same logic doctrine.md documents now extending to fire support and logistics UGVs generally: if a task doesn't require a person physically present, a drone-saturated battlefield gives every reason not to put one there.
